summary.en-US: Hides or marks AI slop on YouTube and any Invidious instance, using the community AiSList channel lists and YouTube's own "altered or synthetic content" label.

description.en-US:
InvidioSlop keeps AI-generated filler out of your video feeds, on YouTube and on any Invidious instance.

**What gets flagged**

- Videos from channels on the AiSList blocklist, a community-maintained list of more than 60,000 channels that mass-produce AI content. Hidden by default.
- Videos from channels on the AiSList warnlist, where AI use is likely but less certain. Marked by default.
- Videos that YouTube itself discloses as AI-made or altered (the "How this was made" label). Marked by default. Videos that are only auto-dubbed are not flagged.

**How it shows up**

- Hidden videos are removed from search results, recommendations, channel pages and Shorts shelves.
- Marked videos stay visible but are desaturated and carry a badge saying why they were flagged.
- If you open a flagged video or channel directly, a dismissible banner tells you. Playback is never blocked.

**You stay in control**

- Choose Hide, Mark or Ignore separately for each of the three categories.
- Keep your own lists of channels to always block or never flag.
- Reveal everything hidden on the current page with one switch in the toolbar popup.

**Works on any Invidious instance**

Invidious is detected from the page itself, so there is no list of instances to maintain. This is why the extension asks for access to all websites; on anything that is not YouTube or Invidious it does nothing.

**Privacy**

- The AiSList files are downloaded from GitHub and refreshed every six hours.
- To match channels and read YouTube's AI label, the extension sends video and channel IDs to youtube.com, without cookies. On Invidious, these requests go directly from your browser to YouTube. You can switch them off in the popup, at the cost of most matching on Invidious and the AI label everywhere.
- Results are cached locally. Nothing is sent to the developer or to any other party.

**Credits**

Channel lists come from the AiSList project (github.com/Override92/AiSList), licensed CC BY-NC 4.0. InvidioSlop is open source under GPL-3.0: github.com/tikaydaes/invidioslop
